chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, from Ali ibn Khalid, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadhl, from Amr ibn Sa'id, from Musaddiq ibn Sadah, from 'Ammar ibn Musa al-Sabati, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
"If a man forgets the Tashahhud in the prayer and remembers that he said 'Bismillah' only, then his prayer is valid. And if he does not remember anything of the Tashahhud, he must repeat the prayer."

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: The meaning in this report is that if he remembers that he said 'Bismillah', his prayer is complete, and he completes the two testimonies (of faith) as a make-up (Qada) and does not repeat the prayer. And if he does not remember anything of the Tashahhud, he repeats the prayer if his leaving it was deliberate. And the report does not specify whether he forgot it or did it deliberately. And if he left it forgetting and then remembered, it is obligatory upon him to make up the Tashahhud, as we have clarified.

key_terms.التَّشَهُّد: Tashahhud (the testimonies of faith recited in prayer)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if one forgets the Tashahhud during prayer?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the fiqh of *nasi* (forgetfulness) regarding the Tashahhud, distinguishing between partial and total omission. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes that recalling even 'Bismillah' validates the prayer with mere compensation (*qada*), whereas total amnesia necessitates repetition (*i'ada*), a ruling refined by scholars to apply primarily to deliberate omission. This highlights the Shia juristic principle that minor forgetfulness does not invalidate the prayer's core validity but requires rectification.
